decisive_items: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin: 128.00 pg/ml initially, peaked at 142.00 pg/ml
Cardiac MRI: Showed slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values, minimal hyperintensity of pericardium without effusion
continuous anterior chest pain exacerbated by deep breathing
response.rationale: Myopericarditis uniquely accounts for both pericardial inflammation (pleuritic chest pain, pericardial hyperintensity) and myocardial injury (elevated troponin, increased T1/T2 mapping, conduction disease), while normal coronary CTA excludes ACS and negative viral serologies/lesion morphology argue against isolated viral myocarditis, Lyme, or syphilis.

rejected.why: Normal coronary CT angiography and pericardial pattern argue against ACS despite troponin elevation.
Negative viral serologies and pericardial hyperintensity make isolated viral myocarditis less likely.
Genital vesicular/umbilicated lesions and lack of erythema migrans/tick exposure do not support Lyme carditis.
Less specific than acute pericarditis and does not explain myocardial injury.
Prior treated syphilis and genital lesions do not explain acute cardiac MRI, troponin, and conduction abnormalities.
